payingUser: A tabletop game master who already pays for DM tooling: 8 of 8 enriched worldbuilding incumbents declare in-app purchases, the 500K+ category leader runs ads plus IAP, and the adjacent name generator earns 4.8 stars over 7,300 reviews.
paidUnit: A permanent themed content pack that adds an authored library of scene parts in one genre; the base app already ships a complete core library, so a pack buys more worlds rather than access to the feature.
momentOfPayment: After the first generated scene, when the user presses Keep to pin that scene to the session board; generation is never interrupted, and the pack is what is sold.
distinctnessSentence: One press returns a whole runnable scene instead of a single table result, every part names its source table and re-rolls in place, the scene stays on the device so nothing is uploaded or server-deleted, no advertisement covers a roll, and the library is bought as permanent packs rather than rented.
day1RevenuePath: A game master generates a scene in the first session, presses Keep, and buys the 2.99 USD base unlock at that moment; a second themed pack follows when the campaign moves to another genre.
assumptionsUnverified: No conversion reading exists: the arithmetic is a threshold, not a forecast, and only a dated Play Console reading through check-outcomes.mjs can decide it.
The shelf monetizes by in-app purchase, but nothing measured shows any incumbent selling genre packs; the repeat unit is this plan's own design and is untested.
The 5-6 agent hour estimate assumes the authored library stays in scope; a larger library than planned is the main schedule risk and the core promise is there to catch it.
The name passed a Play search only; no trademark register was screened, so no legal clearance exists.
